question: A type of outdoor lamp that passes electricity through a gas enclosed in a glass tube to produce 40 to 80 lumens per watt of light is known as a/an: A. incandescent lamp. B. metal-halide lamp. C. halogen lamp. D. fluorescent lamp.

The hazards that security seeks to protect against are commonly divided into which of the following categories of threat? A. Human and systemic B. Man-made and natural C. Internal and external D. Direct and indirect
The badge system in which a badge or pass is coded for authorization to enter specific areas is known as the: A. PIN system. B. pass exchange system. C. multiple-pass system. D. single-pass system.

A security system buyer seeking the best value without technical proposals or alternative solutions would utilize which of the following methods of security systems procurement? A. Invitation for bid B. Request for quote C. Bidder inquiry D. Request for proposal
The optimal lighting type to support color closed-circuit television (CCTV) system effectiveness is: A. mercury vapor. B. metal halide. C. low-pressure sodium vapor. D. high-pressure sodium vapor.

The manager of a multi-tenant office complex is advised to install easily seen emergency call stations and additional lighting to increase illumination in the parking deck. This would follow the crime prevention through environmental design (CPTED) strategy of: A. improving space scheduling. B. overcoming distance and isolation. C. relocating gathering areas. D. redesigning the use of space to provide natural barriers.

A security analyst should do which of the following in situations where a review of past and current crimes for a given site or facility cannot be sampled? A. Restrict the analysis to potential crimes that could be committed at the targeted location. B. Expand the analysis to include petty crimes. C. Expand the analysis to include actual crimes committed outside the targeted location. D. Restrict the analysis to crimes committed within the targeted location.

Which of the following are the stages of the project management? A. Design, development, execution, and closeout B. Design, initiation, implementation, and closeout C. Initiation, development, implementation, and closeout D. Feasibility, development, execution, and closeout
At night, what type of outdoor lighting best reduces risk when going from a brightly lit tennis court to the parking lot? A. Transitional B. Intermittent C. Continuous D. Focused

The basic countermeasures against all forms of lock manipulation are to use close tolerances during manufacture and to: A. use heel-and-toe locking. B. increase the numbers of pins, discs, or levers. C. force misalignment of tumblers. D. use non-sprung positive locking mechanisms.

Which of the following items are part of the planning phase of project management? A. Bidder's instructions and business objectives B. Technical evaluations and equipment lists C. Bidder's conference and cost evaluations D. Threat assessment and design criteria

A well-engineered physical protection system should include: A. protection in depth, minimum consequence of component failure, and balanced protection. B. low cost, protection in depth, and balanced protection. C. protection in depth, balanced protection, and location of the response force. D. minimum consequence of component failure, low cost, and protection in depth.

According to the Physical Protection System project rules of thumb, which of the following will comprise the largest percentage of a system's cost? A. Design and engineering B. Hardware and software C. Installation D. Contingency
Which of the following alarm devices is the best method of protecting a metal container such as a safe or file cabinet? A. Ultrasound B. Capacitance C. Motion detection D. Vibration detection

The critical detection point on a given path is defined as the point where: A. the adversary is closer to the asset than to the outermost protective layer. B. any sensor detects the presence of the adversary. C. the adversary is closer to success than defeat. D. the delay time remaining exceeds the response force time.

Which of the following lists includes only volumetric sensors? A. Seismic pressure, microwave, and electric field B. Capacitance, passive infrared, and electric field C. Video motion, magnetic field, and microwave D. Vibration, fiber optic cable, and ultrasonic

A security consultant is charged with designing security measures for a new facility. To ensure maximum effectiveness, the system should be designed: A. during construction and before occupancy. B. at the inception of the project. C. with pre-specified equipment in mind. D. as part of the request for proposal (RFP) process.
What testing type determines if components performed as expected? A. Functional B. Stress C. Commissioning D. Verification

When conducting an analysis of threatened targets, the prioritization of targets should be based on the: A. risk to the asset. B. consequence of the loss. C. probability of the loss. D. threat to the asset.
Which of the following is not a principal source of information for a threat analysis? A. Intelligence sources B. Professional organizations C. Crime analysis D. Employee reports
In order for a poured concrete vault to protect against forced entry, the walls, ceiling, and floor must be at least how many inches thick? A. 6 B. 10 C. 12 D. 24
A lock assembly that is projected by a spring action and retracted by either end pressure or a lever is known as a/an: A. intermittent deadbolt. B. latchbolt. C. positive deadbolt. D. deadlatch.
Electromechanical sensors are: A. line, visible, and sense volume changes. B. vibrations, visible, and line. C. vibration, line, and proximity. D. passive, visible, and line.
A reliability test should be conducted 24 hours a day for how many consecutive days? A. 7 B. 14 C. 15 D. 30

The first requirement for a life-safety and security protection of high-rise structures is that: A. a comprehensive emergency management plan is created. B. evacuations signs are posted within each egress stairwell with adequate lighting. C. contact details are conspicuously posted for persons and agencies needed in an emergency. D. floor wardens have the required protective gear that allows them to ensure that offices are empty before they evacuate.
The role that introduces artificial stimuli in a business continuity test and exercise process is known as the: A. simulator. B. controller. C. observer. D. participant.
Electromagnetic locks should generate a minimum holding force of: A. 300 pounds. B. 600 pounds. C. 900 pounds. D. 1200 pounds.

Each specification section consists of a standard format divided into what three parts? A. General, products, and execution B. Design, products, and execution C. Design, execution, and maintenance D. General, design, and execution

A consultant is designing security measures for a convenience store. Which of the following would be the most appropriate for reducing criminal activity using basic crime prevention through environmental design (CPTED) strategies? A. Placing security stickers in the front windows B. Putting public telephones as close to the front entrance as possible C. Installing very high display racks D. Placing parking in front of the store

After establishing the objectives and developing the design for the physical protection system at a high-security facility, the design effectiveness should be evaluated by using: A. qualitative analysis. B. quantitative analysis. C. threat and vulnerability analysis. D. performance verification analysis.

System integration requires a balance among which of the following elements? A. Hardware, personnel, and operational procedures B. Exterior sensors, interior sensors, and alarm panels C. Camera systems, access control systems, and central station monitoring systems D. Hardware, access control systems, and operational procedures
Which of the following phases of project deliverables includes system specifications, evaluation criteria, and the implementation schedule? A. Procurement B. Planning C. Installation D. Design
